Axiom: **Bootstrap Requirements rows with Owner=`this-scope-task` aggregate into the minimum number of tickets per `AX_DAG_AND_TICKET_BOUNDARIES`.** Default — group by Resolution affinity (all `package` rows → one «install deps» ticket; all `structural` rows editing the same config file → one ticket); subdivide only when (P) parallel-executable or (C) context overflow. Source: scope spec Bootstrap Requirements (infrastructure 9, contracts 7, library 8, product 8). Each emitted node carries its closed owner kind: infrastructure rows → `infrastructure-flat`; product/library `this-scope-task` rows → `scope-bootstrap`; product/library module work → `module`. No fourth owner exists; interface never owns a task. - Rows with Owner=`external-prereq-scope` → cross-scope dependency edge, not a ticket here. - Rows with Owner=`operator-action` → noted in tracker index as a blocking external prerequisite, not a ticket. - Bootstrap tickets must be DONE before any non-bootstrap ticket of the same scope (e.g. `install package` precedes `wire config that uses package`). - Package/tool rows materialize one explicit dependency provider phase: `Bootstrap Action: dependency-install`, `Provides Packages: `, and Target Files containing both `package.json` and the active clean-HEAD lockfile. Every phase that needs those tools declares `Requires Packages:` and its ticket depends forward on that provider. Provider→consumer reverse edges and cycles are invalid; a later “install deps” ticket cannot rescue an earlier config/gate ticket. - Bootstrap tickets carry Verification populated from the Resolution column (e.g. `npm ls ` exit 0) — ONE `npm ls ` call PER package, never a single `npm ls pkg1 pkg2 ...` covering several: a multi-package call can exit 0 as soon as one of the named packages resolves, silently masking an absent one among the rest (observed with a missing optional-peer package, e.g. `@vitest/coverage-v8`, riding alongside a resolved `vitest` in the same call) — the gate passes while a real dependency is missing. One call per package makes that package's own absence surface as that call's own non-zero exit, with nowhere to hide behind a sibling that did resolve. - **Every shared infra file — `package.json` plus its active lockfile, scripts, `.nvmrc`, a tool config a bootstrap ticket creates or edits — gets EXACTLY ONE ticket-owner: the bootstrap ticket whose Target Files list it.** Any OTHER ticket whose phase reads or extends that same file (adds a script, bumps the pinned tool version) does not re-derive ownership by grepping neighboring tickets — its phase text carries an explicit line naming the owner, `владелец — ` (or `owner — `), written at scaffold time, so the worker executing that phase already knows whose ticket to defer to / coordinate with without a search. - If Bootstrap Requirements is absent from the spec → abort with `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING` (the spec did not pass discovery STEP_7).
